situation: I'm the hiring manager. Need to reject Daniel, a finalist for our senior marketing role; his launch plan presentation on Thursday was great, but the other candidate has B2B SaaS experience. We'll likely open a consumer marketing lead role in spring. I called him, now I need the follow-up email.
reply: Hi Daniel, thanks again for the time you gave us, especially the launch plan you presented on Thursday, which the team is still talking about. As I said on the phone, we've offered the role to another candidate whose background is in B2B SaaS, which is where most of this role's work sits. It was a close decision. If we open the consumer marketing lead role in the spring, I'd like to contact you first, if you're open to that. Best, Farah
note: Only offer the spring role if it's real; a door left open falsely is worse than none.

situation: 手上有两个offer，决定去另一家了，要拒绝这家的HR张女士。面试时跟他们的李总聊得很好，不想把关系弄僵。
reply: 张女士您好，非常感谢您和团队这段时间的安排，特别是和李总聊的那一轮，聊得非常愉快。经过慎重考虑，我决定接受另一家公司的offer。这个决定并不容易。希望以后还有机会合作，也祝团队一切顺利。
note: 不编理由也不说对方哪里不好，“接受了另一家的offer”本身就是完整的真实理由；点名感谢具体的人。

situation: Un chasseur de têtes, Julien, m'écrit sur LinkedIn pour un poste de directeur financier dans une PME à Lyon. Je suis bien dans mon poste et je ne veux pas bouger avant au moins un an, mais j'aimerais garder le contact.
reply: Bonjour Julien, merci pour votre message et d'avoir pensé à moi. Je ne suis pas à l'écoute du marché en ce moment : je me plais dans mon poste actuel et je compte y rester au moins un an. N'hésitez pas à me recontacter l'an prochain, j'aurai plaisir à en reparler.
note: Un non clair dès la deuxième phrase, une raison vraie, et une porte ouverte avec une échéance précise, parce qu'elle l'est vraiment.

situation: I'm in the final round for a data analyst role at Northfen Energy, panel is this Thursday. My current company just offered me the internal transfer I've wanted for a year and I've accepted. The recruiter is Nadia.
reply:
Hi Nadia,
Thank you for the time you and the team have put into this, especially the earlier rounds, which I really enjoyed. I want to tell you early rather than late: I'm withdrawing from the process, so please do release Thursday's panel slot. I've accepted an internal move at my current company that I've been working toward for a while, and it wouldn't be fair to keep taking your team's time. I'd be glad to stay in touch.
Best,
Priya
note: Withdraw before the panel, not after it: the decision by the second sentence, the true reason in one line, and freeing the slot as the practical ask.

situation: 我是技术经理，组里的高级工程师小吴申请了内部的技术主管岗位，最后我们选了外部候选人。他技术很强，但这个岗位要直接带8个人，他带人经验还不够；下季度支付重构小组可以让他牵头带两三个人。明天当面谈，谈完想再给他发一条消息。
reply: 小吴，谢谢你今天愿意坐下来聊，也谢谢你为这次竞聘准备的架构方案，写得非常扎实。就像当面说的，技术主管这次选了外部候选人，主要是这个岗位一上来就要带8个人，需要更多带团队的经验。这不影响我对你技术能力的判断。如果你愿意，下个季度我们让你牵头支付重构那个小组，先带两三个人，明年再有机会时你会更有底气。有什么想法，随时找我。
note: 内部候选人要先当面说，再用书面补充：理由真实具体，给一个真实的下一步，而不是空泛的“以后还有机会”。

situation: I'm hiring for a junior accountant. I rejected Ben after the second interview and he emailed back asking for detailed feedback, saying he thinks he was a strong fit. The one real issue: two balances in his reconciliation exercise didn't tie out.
reply: Hi Ben, I understand it's disappointing, and I appreciate you asking directly. The one specific thing I'd point to is the reconciliation exercise: two of the balances didn't tie out, and that kind of accuracy is most of this role day to day. The decision is final, but it's a skill that sharpens quickly with practice, and I wish you the best with the search. Best, Farah
note: A candidate who pushes back gets one more specific point you can defend, then the decision repeated kindly. Don't reopen it or promise a future role you aren't planning.

situation: Got an offer from Tidewell Health for a product manager role at $118k base. My current job pays $130k with bonus and I'd genuinely accept at $130k. The recruiter, Leah, wants an answer by Friday.
reply: Hi Leah, thank you for the offer and for the time the team put into the process. I'd like to be transparent: the base is the one thing stopping me. At $130,000 I'd accept today, since that's what I'd be leaving behind. If there's no flexibility, I completely understand, and I'll decline with genuine thanks by Friday 2 October.
note: Only name a number you would actually sign at. This is the real condition, not a bluff, so be ready to say yes if they meet it.

situation: I verbally accepted an operations analyst offer from Coastline Logistics last Thursday, start date Oct 19, but haven't signed anything. Yesterday the company I've wanted for years made me an offer and I took it. I need to email the hiring manager, Greg, today and I feel awful.
reply:
Hi Greg,
I'm writing to withdraw my acceptance of the operations analyst role. Yesterday I received an offer from a company I've wanted to work for for years, and I've accepted it. I know I said yes to you on Thursday, and backing out now costs you time and a start date you'd planned around, so I wanted you to hear it today rather than later. Thank you for the time you and Renee put into the process; the warehouse walk-through was the best part of any interview I've had. I'm sorry for the disruption, and I wish you and the team the best.
Kind regards,
Maya
note: Reneging on a verbal yes: tell them the day you decide, name the cost to them, and give the true reason rather than a softer invented one. Call first if you can, then send this.

situation: I'm hiring a marketing coordinator. My friend Nicole referred her former colleague Jamie, who interviewed last Wednesday. Jamie was warm and really organised, but we're going with someone with more paid social experience. We'll probably hire an events assistant next spring and Jamie would suit it. I don't want this to feel awkward.
reply: Hi Jamie, thank you for coming in last Wednesday; you were warm and really organised throughout. We've decided to offer the role to another candidate whose background is heavier on paid social, which is the biggest part of the job this year. That was the deciding factor, not how you came across. We're likely to hire an events assistant next spring, and if you'd be open to it, I'd like to reach out to you directly when that opens.
note: A referred candidate gets the same clear, specific no as anyone else. Tell Jamie first, and give Nicole only the outcome, never the interview details.

situation: I'm hiring a UX designer. Elena did a checkout redesign take-home and a final interview on Aug 20, and I told her she'd hear within two weeks. It's been almost six weeks because our budget sign-off stalled, and we've now hired someone with more design systems experience. I need to email her today.
reply:
Hi Elena,
Thank you for the time you put into the process, especially the checkout redesign, which the whole panel talked about afterwards. We've decided to offer the role to another candidate whose background is closer to our design systems work. I also told you you'd hear within two weeks, and it's been almost six. That's on me, and I'm sorry for leaving you waiting. Good luck with the search; the right team will be lucky to have you.
Best,
Marcus
note: A late rejection still leads with the decision, then one plain line owning the delay. Skip the budget saga; it explains your side, not hers.

situation: My close friend Aaron offered me head of operations at his 12-person startup, Pantry, after two long dinners pitching it. I'm staying at my job at Meridian for at least another year. I want to say no without it getting weird between us.
reply: Aaron, thank you for the offer, and for those two dinners walking me through the plan for Pantry; I can tell how much thought has gone into it. I'm going to say no. I'm staying at Meridian for at least another year, and you deserve someone who's all in from day one. I think what you're building is really good, and if you ever want a second pair of eyes on an ops problem, I'm a phone call away.
note: With a friend the no still comes early, the reason is about your timing rather than their company, and you only offer help you'd actually give.

situation: 我是一家贸易公司的部门经理，老板把他外甥小赵的简历转给我，让我“看看合不合适”。外贸专员这个岗位要求三年经验，他刚毕业，我面了一轮决定不录用。他对市场挺有感觉，明年春天公司可能招管培生，他很合适。要给小赵本人发邮件。
reply: 小赵你好，谢谢你来面谈。这次外贸专员的岗位我们决定不录用：这个岗位一上来就要独立跟海外客户，需要至少三年的外贸经验，这是岗位的硬要求。你对市场的敏感度很不错，明年春天如果公司开放管培生岗位，我会第一时间告诉你。祝求职顺利。
note: 关系户也按正常标准拒，信里只讲岗位要求；跟老板那边另外单独说明，不写进给候选人的信里。

situation: 领导刘总想提拔我做组长，带5个人，下个月生效。我想继续做技术，不想带人。我们关系不错，不想让他觉得我不上进。
reply: 刘总，谢谢您考虑让我做组长，被您这样信任我很感激。这几天我认真想过了，决定不接这个岗位：接下来两三年我还是想专心做技术。这个岗位对团队很重要，我更希望由真正想带人的同事来做。组长我不接，但技术上需要我多扛的，您尽管交给我。
note: 拒绝上级的提拔：先感谢、第二句就给决定，理由讲自己想走的方向而不是岗位不好，再说清楚愿意在哪方面多出力。

situation: Ich habe die Zusage für eine Promotionsstelle bei Prof. Hartmann in der Hydrologie-Arbeitsgruppe der Uni Freiburg. Ich habe mich aber für ein Angebot der ETH Zürich entschieden. Er hat sich sehr für mich eingesetzt, und in unserem Fach begegnet man sich auf Konferenzen immer wieder.
reply:
Sehr geehrter Herr Professor Hartmann,
vielen Dank für das Angebot und dafür, wie sehr Sie sich für mich eingesetzt haben. Nach langer Überlegung habe ich mich entschieden, die Stelle nicht anzunehmen, und werde meine Promotion an der ETH Zürich beginnen. Ich sage Ihnen das so früh wie möglich, damit Sie die Stelle weiter vergeben können. Die Entscheidung ist mir nicht leichtgefallen, und ich würde mich freuen, Sie und Ihre Gruppe auf einer der nächsten Tagungen wiederzusehen.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Lena Hoffmann
note: In der Wissenschaft sieht man sich wieder: schnell absagen, der ehrliche Grund in einem Halbsatz, und die Tür nur so weit öffnen, wie sie wirklich offen ist.

situation: 我是自由译者，出版社编辑周老师约我翻译一本30万字的英文历史书，明年3月底交稿。我明年上半年的档期已经排满，接不了。之前和她合作过两本书，想以后还能合作。
reply: 周老师您好，谢谢您想到我。这次我没办法接：明年上半年的档期已经排满，30万字3月底交稿，我接了只会耽误书的进度。和您合作的两本书都很愉快，如果明年下半年有合适的选题，很希望您再想着我。
note: 自由职业者拒绝约稿：先感谢，第二句就说不接，理由只给真实的一个，门只开到确实开着的程度。

situation: I resigned yesterday to join a climate nonprofit, with four weeks' notice. Today my manager, Priya, came back with a counteroffer: a 15% raise and the team lead title. It's not about money or title, and I want to say no by email without burning the bridge.
reply: Hi Priya, thank you for the counteroffer, and for putting it together so quickly; the team lead title means a lot coming from you. My decision isn't about pay or title, it's about wanting to work on climate full time, so I'm going to hold to it. I'll make the next four weeks a proper handover, and I'd really like to stay in touch.
note: Answer the counter once and close it; the handover line keeps the last month good.

situation: 青葉大学経済学部4年の佐藤美咲です。第一志望の会社から内定が出たので、先に内定をもらっていた食品メーカーを辞退します。人事の山本さんは面接のたびに声をかけて緊張をほぐしてくれて、社員の方との座談会も組んでくれました。明日10月1日の内定式の前にメールで伝えたいです。
reply:
山本様
いつも大変お世話になっております。青葉大学経済学部の佐藤美咲です。
このたびは内定のご連絡をいただき、誠にありがとうございました。熟慮の末、誠に勝手ながら内定を辞退させていただきたく、ご連絡いたしました。別の会社からも内定をいただき、そちらに入社することを決めました。
面接のたびに山本様がお声がけくださり、社員の方との座談会まで設けていただいたこと、心から感謝しております。内定式を明日に控えた時期のご連絡となり、大変申し訳ございません。
貴社の今後ますますのご発展をお祈り申し上げます。
佐藤美咲
note: 内定式が明日なので、メールを送ったら山本さんに電話でも一言伝えると確実で丁寧です。

situation: I'm a hiring manager. On Sept 16 we offered Farah Haddad a data engineer role and she accepted; she told me she'd hand in her notice at her current job this Friday, Oct 2. This morning the company froze all new hiring until at least April and HR confirmed the offer is withdrawn. It's nothing to do with her, she was our first choice and I'd want to call her first if the freeze lifts. I phoned her an hour ago and now need the follow-up email.
reply: Hi Farah, following up in writing on our call this morning. We have withdrawn the data engineer offer we made on Sept 16, because the company froze all new hiring this morning until at least April. It has nothing to do with you, you were our first choice, and I'm sorry to undo something you'd already said yes to. Please don't hand in your notice on Friday on our account. If the freeze lifts, would it be okay for me to contact you first?
note: Send it before she acts on the offer. Questions about pay or the offer terms go to HR; check the offer letter rather than guessing.

situation: I run a café. Jess did a paid trial shift last Saturday; the regulars loved her, but she struggled on the espresso machine in the rush, and the job means running the bar alone on weekday mornings. Her £48 for the trial goes out with Friday's pay run, and we may hire weekend front-of-house in spring, when I'd happily call her. I want to text her.
reply: Hi Jess, thanks for Saturday's trial shift, the regulars really took to you. We've decided not to offer you the role. The job means running the espresso bar alone on weekday mornings, and the rush showed that part isn't quite there yet. We may hire weekend front-of-house in the spring, and if we do I'd like to call you. Your £48 for Saturday goes out with Friday's pay run.
note: A text suits a trial shift; the one reason is the one she saw for herself on the day.

situation: I'm hiring a customer support lead. I did a phone screen with Aaron Mills yesterday; he's strong and his team-building story was great, but he needs a base of $95,000 and our band for the role tops out at $82,000, which can't move. I want to email him today.
reply: Hi Aaron, thank you for the call yesterday, especially your team-building story, which was a great answer. We won't be moving forward, and I want to be straight about why: you mentioned a base of $95,000, and our band for this role tops out at $82,000 with no flexibility. That's about our budget, not your experience. I wish you the best with the search.
note: When the reason is the salary band, say the number plainly; it's the most useful feedback he can get, and the door stays closed because it is.

situation: I'm the hiring manager for head of science at Westbrook School. Tomorrow at 4 I'm phoning Priyanka, one of two finalists, to tell her we've chosen the other finalist, mainly because they've already led a science department. Her demo lesson on electrolysis was the best we saw. What do I actually say on the call?
reply: Hi Priyanka, it's Daniel from Westbrook School, thanks for picking up. I wanted to tell you myself rather than by email: we've offered the head of science role to the other finalist. It came down to them having already led a science department, which is a big part of this job from day one. Your electrolysis lesson was the best demo lesson we saw. I'll follow up with a short email today, and if you have any questions now, I'm happy to answer them.
note: On the phone, the decision goes in the first breath after hello; the positive and the questions come after, never before.

situation: I run a small agency. Marta has freelanced for us as a copywriter for two years and applied for our new in-house content lead role; we've hired someone who has already managed a team, which the role needs from day one and she hasn't done. I'm telling her on a call tomorrow and then need the follow-up email. I want to keep sending her freelance work, starting with the Halden brochure next month.
reply: Hi Marta, thank you for putting yourself forward for the content lead role, and for the care you put into the application. As I said on the call, we've offered it to someone who has already managed a team, which the role needs from day one. That's no comment on your writing, which is exactly why clients keep asking for you. I'd really like to keep working together, starting with the Halden brochure next month, if you're up for it.
note: When the working relationship continues, say so concretely, and only because it is true.

situation: I'm hiring an office manager. Gavin interviewed with me on Tuesday and clearly knew his stuff on running office budgets, but when he arrived he snapped at our receptionist, Lena, over the parking instructions. We won't be hiring him or considering him again, and I need a short rejection email.
reply: Hi Gavin, thank you for coming in on Tuesday and for the detail you gave on running office budgets. We've decided not to move forward with your application. This role works closely with everyone in the office, and the exchange at reception when you arrived weighed in our decision. I wish you the best with your search.
note: The door is closed, so no stay-in-touch line; if he disputes it, restate the decision once and close.

situation: I'm hiring a bookkeeper for our small accounting firm. After Mei's second interview on Sept 24 I told her on the way out that she was 'very likely our pick', but the partners then chose a candidate with a payroll certification, which the role needs for our new payroll clients. Her spreadsheet test was the cleanest we saw, and I need to email her today and own that I got ahead of myself.
reply: Hi Mei, thank you for the time you gave us, and for your spreadsheet test, which was the cleanest we saw. We've decided to offer the role to another candidate who holds a payroll certification, which the role needs for our new payroll clients. I also told you on 24 September that you were very likely our pick, and I shouldn't have said that before the decision was made. I'm sorry for the hope it gave you. I wish you the best with your search.
note: Own the premature signal in one plain line after the decision; skip the story of how the partners decided.

situation: 我之前跟北京一家公司的HR王女士说过，月薪到3万5我就接，今天他们真的批了3万5。但这周我爱人确定下个月调去成都工作，我们决定一起搬过去，这个北京的岗位我去不了了。面试时技术总监孙总花了很多时间跟我聊团队规划，我很过意不去。
reply: 王女士您好，非常感谢您和孙总为这个offer花的心思，也谢谢公司批了3万5的月薪，这正是我之前提的数字。我必须坦白告诉您：这周家里情况有变，我爱人确定下个月调到成都工作，我们决定一起搬过去，所以北京的这个岗位我没办法接了，这和薪资无关。在您帮我争取到条件之后才这样说，真的很抱歉。和孙总聊团队规划是整个面试里最让我受启发的一段，希望以后还有机会合作。
note: 对方满足了你提的条件之后再拒绝，要讲清真实原因并明说与条件无关，道歉一次就够；对方再加价也不要重新谈。

situation: 我拿到一家互联网公司的产品经理offer，HR是陈女士。终面时部门负责人全程看手机、打断我好几次，我不想进这个团队，但也不想在回复里指责谁。一面的面试官小杨人很好，跟我聊了很多用户研究的实践。
reply: 陈女士您好，谢谢您和团队这几周的安排，也谢谢一面时小杨跟我聊了那么多用户研究的实践，收获很大。经过考虑，我决定不接受这个产品经理的offer。谢谢您一路的沟通，祝团队一切顺利。
note: 真实原因说出来只会伤人时，可以不给理由，但不要编一个；她追问的话，说“团队的工作方式和我想要的不太一致”就够了。

situation: 我们家在找住家阿姨带两岁的女儿朵朵。李阿姨试工了三天，做饭很好吃，朵朵也喜欢她，但我们夫妻俩经常出差，最后选了另一位有育婴师证、能长期住家的阿姨。说好的试工费每天300元，一共900元，我今天转给她。想发微信告诉她。
reply: 李阿姨您好，这三天辛苦您了，您做的饭全家都爱吃，朵朵也很喜欢您。我们商量后，决定请另一位阿姨长期带朵朵：我们俩经常出差，最后选了有育婴师证、能长期住家的那位。三天的试工费900元我今天转给您。真心谢谢您这几天的照顾，祝您早点找到合适的人家。
note: 家里请人也是拒绝候选人：前两句就给决定，理由只讲选人的标准，不评价她本人，试工费当天结清。

situation: 我在一家证券研究所实习了六个月，带我的是陈姐，今天HR林女士给了我转正offer。但我已经决定明年去英国读硕士，录取通知上周到了。陈姐这半年手把手教我写行业报告，我很感激，以后也想有机会再合作。
reply: 林女士您好，非常感谢公司给我转正的机会，也感谢这半年的培养。考虑之后，我决定不接受这份offer：我已经拿到英国一个硕士项目的录取，明年去读书。这半年陈姐手把手带我写行业报告，是我实习里收获最大的部分，我也会当面再跟她道谢。希望以后还有机会合作，祝团队一切顺利。
note: 实习转正的offer也要尽快、明确地拒绝；感谢落到带你的具体的人身上，留门的话要是真心的。

situation: Recebi a proposta da Vértice Engenharia para analista de projetos. Nas entrevistas, a gestora, Carla, falou em modelo híbrido com três dias em casa, mas a carta veio com trabalho 100% presencial, e o RH, Rodrigo, confirmou que isso não vai mudar. Moro a duas horas do escritório, então vou recusar, mas gostei muito das conversas com a Carla.
reply: Olá, Rodrigo. Agradeço a proposta e por ter confirmado a questão do modelo de trabalho. Depois de pensar bem, decidi não aceitar a vaga de analista de projetos. Como moro a duas horas do escritório, o formato 100% presencial não funciona para mim. As conversas com a Carla foram das melhores do processo, e peço que agradeça a ela por mim. Desejo muito sucesso à equipe.
note: O motivo real em uma frase, sem acusar a empresa de ter mudado as condições; como o RH já disse que não muda, não há o que negociar.

situation: I'm an engineering manager at Lumen Freight. Sara Kim was on my team for three years and left on good terms in 2024 to join a startup; she applied for our new team lead role and interviewed last Friday. We've offered it to someone who has already run on-call for a team of eight, which the role needs from day one; her system design round was excellent, and I'd genuinely rehire her as a senior engineer.
reply: Hi Sara, thank you for coming back to interview with us last Friday; it was really good to see you again, and your system design round was excellent. We've decided to offer the team lead role to someone who has already run on-call for a team of eight, which the role needs from day one. That's about this role, not about you. If you'd ever like to rejoin us as a senior engineer, I'd be glad to talk, and I mean that.
note: A former colleague gets the same early, clear no as anyone else, plus a door you would really open; call her first if you can.

situation: 我是一家电商公司的HR主管。运营岗候选人周婷终面后我们没有录用，选了另一位有跨境电商经验的候选人，这是岗位的核心要求；周婷做的活动策划案很出色。她今天在微信上问我：“是不是因为我面试时说今年刚结婚？”婚育情况在我们的评估里完全没有涉及，也没有影响决定。
reply: 周婷你好，谢谢你直接来问，我理解你会这样想。我可以明确告诉你：你的婚姻状况和这次的决定没有任何关系，我们的评估里也完全没有涉及。决定的原因是这个岗位的核心是跨境电商运营，另一位候选人在这方面有直接经验。你的活动策划案是这次面试里最出色的之一。这次的结果不会改变，祝你早日找到合适的机会。
note: 候选人怀疑被区别对待时，不辩解、不生气，正面回答再重申真实理由；她若要正式投诉，按公司流程转给负责人并如实记录。

situation: I'm hiring a front-end developer. I rejected Marcus after four rounds, and he replied angrily that we 'wasted his time' with a take-home that took him six hours. He has a point: our brief said three to four hours, and that estimate was too low. The decision stands, and the specific reason was that his take-home had no tests, which this role relies on every day.
reply: Hi Marcus, that's fair feedback about the take-home. Our brief said three to four hours, that estimate was too low, and I'm sorry it cost you six; I'm making sure the brief gets fixed. The decision is final, and the one specific thing behind it is that your take-home didn't include tests, which this role relies on every day. Thank you for the time you put in, and I wish you the best with the search.
note: Concede the part he's right about in one line, give one defensible reason, then hold the decision and close.

situation: I'm hiring a junior UX designer at Fernbrook, a small app studio. Olivia Grant, a primary school teacher changing careers, applied with a cover letter about redesigning her school's parent portal. For this round we're only interviewing people who have already shipped work on a live app, and she hasn't yet; I want to send a short, personal rejection.
reply: Hi Olivia, thank you for applying for the junior UX designer role at Fernbrook, and for your cover letter about redesigning your school's parent portal, which was a genuinely good read. We're not moving forward with your application this time. For this round we're only interviewing people who have already shipped work on a live app, which isn't a comment on your ability. I hope you find the right fit soon.
note: At the application stage, one detail from her letter proves it was read, and the shortlist rule is the honest reason; no 'CV on file' unless you'll use it.

situation: I'm hiring a warehouse operations supervisor, and an agency recruiter, Tom Price at Kestrelway Staffing, sent us his candidate Leon, who interviewed on Tuesday. Leon's answer on the safety walk-through was the best we heard, but we've chosen someone who has already run a night shift, which this role needs from day one. I want to email Tom today so he can tell Leon, with feedback he can pass on.
reply: Hi Tom, thanks for sending Leon our way, and please thank him for coming in on Tuesday. We've decided not to offer him the operations supervisor role. We've gone with a candidate who has already run a night shift, which this role needs from day one. Feedback you're welcome to pass on: his answer on the safety walk-through was the best we heard from anyone. Could you let him know today?
note: Through an agency, write the decision, the one reason and one real positive in words the recruiter can pass on unchanged.
